This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondents for the relief of
compensation under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989.
Scch 5
2.

The brief facts of case of the Petitioner is as under:
That on 16

.07.2017 at about 6.30 p.m. while moving on his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA41V3441 towards CMTI Junction carefully and cautiously, a Mahendra Logan Car bearing Reg.No.KA04C8831 came in high speed rash and negligently on back side and dashed against him, due to the said accident, he fell down and sustained multiple grievous injuries on hip and both legs and taken first aid at Bengaluru Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, thereafter shifted to ESIC Medical Colleger, PGIMSR and Model Hospital, took treatment as indoor patient for 6 days, thereafter he has taken followup treatment, for that spent an amount of Rs.2,00,000/ towards medicine and hospital charges, Rs.65,000/ towards conveyance and nourishment SCCH 5 charges, he needs further surgery which costs Rs.50,000/.
3.

entities.text: ESIC Medical Colleger, PGIMSR and Model Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
At the time of accident, he was aged about 24 years, working as Production Asst. Trainee at M/s.
General Electronics Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru, thereby earning Rs.10,000/ to Rs.12,000/ p.m., due to this accident, he has lost his work and income.
Out of the said accident, crime No.265/2017 is registered before Yeshwanthpura Traffic police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.

R1 is owner, R2 is insurer of said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner, so that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, R1/owner has not appeared, hence placed exparte.

R2/insurer has appeared and filed SCCH 5 written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, wherein taken contention that, petitioner has to prove all the allegations about negligency and cause of the accident, further petitioner has to prove his age and income, petitioner has to prove that he had valid driving license at the time of accident, R1 has to prove the compliance of policy conditions, if policy conditions are Sri. Nithin S.N vs Sri. Munaaf on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42432639/
2 complied then only he is ready to indemnify the same, claim made by the petitioner is higher side,
hence petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::

1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on SCCH 5 16.07.2017 at about 6.30 p.m. near CMTI Junction, Tumkur Road, Yeshwanthpura, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of Mahindra Logan Car bearing Reg.No.KA04C8831 by its driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1 and marked 11 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, R2 has deposed her evidence as RW1 and marked 5 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5 and closed her evidence.
SCCH 5 7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1: As per the case of the petitioner, very accident is occurred on 16.07.2017 at about 6.30 p.m. near CMTI Junction, very car has dashed against his motor cycle on back side, said fact is not disputed by the R2.
Further there is dispute by the R2 that, there is no negligency of the car driver and he has not dashed against the motor cycle.
9. In this regard there is crossexamination by counsel for R2 denying the negligency of the car driver, SCCH 5 but PW1 has denied his suggestions.
Even R1/owner has not at all contested the petition, not examined the driver of the said car in this case.

10. On the other hand, R2 has deposed her evidence as RW1 and deposed her evidence denying Sri. Nithin S.N vs Sri. Munaaf on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42432639/
3 case of the petitioner.

sentences.text:
She has furnished copy of policy marked as Ex.R.1, copy of charge sheet marked as Ex.R.2, authorization letter marked as Ex.R.3, copy of Sec.133 Notice marked as Ex.R.4 and copy of reply marked as Ex.R.5.
11.

The police papers marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 speaks that, very FIR and charge sheet are against the said car and driver, it goes to show that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver, but not by the negligency of the motor cyclist.
Hence believing the version of the petitioner and disbelieving the version of SCCH 5 the respondent, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
very accident
is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.
Hence I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
As per the case of the petitioner, he had sustained fracture lower shaft of tibia and fibula.
In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5 issued by ESIC Medical College, PGIMSR and Model Hospital.
It is noticed that, there is no discharge summary on record to know that, how many days he has taken treatment and what kind of treatment is given to the petitioner.

Further he has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.9 amounting to Rs.13,077/,
but in support of the same there are no medical prescriptions.
Further there is no evidence of Doctor to know the nature of the injuries sustained by SCCH 5 the petitioner, treatment taken by him and disability suffered by him.
13. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 24 years as on the date of accident.

In order to prove his age, petitioner has produced copy of driving license marked as Ex.P.11, accordingly he is born on 01.09.1995, very accident is occurred on 16.07.2017, considering Ex.P.11, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner at 22 years as on the date of accident.
As per the case of the petitioner, he was working as Production Asst. Trainee at M/s. General Electronics Pvt. Ltd., thereby earning Rs.10,000/ to Rs.12,000/ p.m.

In support of his earnings, he has furnished appointment letter marked as Ex.P.8 issued by GE BE Private Ltd., wherein his salary is mentioned as Rs.13,000/ p.m. further he has produced bank statement marked as SCCH 5 Ex.P.10.

On perusal of the same it reveals that, he has made some financial transactions, but there is no entry about receipt of payment, however when there is no medical evidence to prove the injuries and surgery and when there is no discharge summary, under such circumstances, this tribunal is of the opinion that,
petitioner has failed to prove the injuries caused and treatment taken by him.

Under such circumstances, this tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled only for medical bills of Rs.13,077/ along with global compensation of Rs.30,000/.
14.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.43,077/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
SCCH 5 15.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.072800311P111993139, which is valid for the period from 13.12.2016 to 12.12.2017, the alleged accident was occurred on 16.07.2017, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force, which is marked as Ex.R.1.

Further on perusal of the Ex.P.7 charge sheet it is noticed that,

driver of the car had no driving license at the time of accident, petitioner has not produced the same,
owner of the vehicle is placed exparte.
16. In crossexamination it is clearly mentioned that, driver of the car had no driving license at the time of accident, with regard to this Sec.3 R/w. Sec.181 of M.V.Act is entered in charge sheet.
Hence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, driver of the car had no driving license at the time of accident.
SCCH 5 17.
Under such circumstances, naturally R1/owner is liable to pay the compensation in favour of petitioner, but

as per the observations made and findings given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s. Swarna Singh and other reported in AIR 2004 SC 1531 and in case of Pappu and another V/s. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another reported in AIR 2018 SC 592, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to issue directions against R2 Insurance Company to satisfy the petitioner by way of depositing the award amount within 60 days from the date of this order with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and recover from the R1/owner through process of law.

SCCH 5 18. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.43,077/
(Rupees Forty Three Thousand Seventy Seven Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order and recover from the respondent No.1/owner with due process of law.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through epayment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.

The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
SCCH 5 Draw award accordingly.
